Category: Mountain
Description: The clearing outside of the cave is very small and rocky. Only about four or five people can fit it if they squeeze. The ground is very rough and covered with plant life. There are also a few trees growing in the mouth of the cave, to the east of the tiny clearing, meaning people have to slip between the trees to get into the cave. This makes it easier to hide, because the people will drag brush to the cave mouth and make it look like it has fallen there naturally, blocking the existence of the cave at all. The clearing is both very convenient as it makes an excellent hiding place, and very inconvenient because it is very hard to get people through the clearing and into the cave quickly in an emergency.
Background: This cave was a backup emergency hiding place. Originally people would evacuate to a larger cave, but that one was discovered by an enemy, and the people hiding in it were killed. Luckily, some people had gotten lost, and stumbled upon this cave. They barely made it into the cave before the enemy was upon them, and luckily in the dark the enemy thought the space was too small for anyone to be hiding and missed the cave entirely. Ever since, people have gone to this cave in emergencies.

[Setting]

Description: Opening the large stonework doors at the top of the grand staircase reveals the prized artifacts stored within the top floor of the palace. Inside are trinkets and baubles from far off lands, souvenirs from expeditions traversing across the entire realm. Large animal hides, beautiful tapestries, intricate statues of mythical animals, and other treasures hang upon thick oaken scaffolds. A thick coat of dust covers much of the treasure, suggesting a long absence of human contact or disruption.
Background: The owner of the palace cherished his wife more than anything in the world, and these artifacts stored in the top floor of the palace were a testament to his love. He sent his emissaries far and wide to collect them, hoping to find something as beautiful as she was, something to prove his love to her.  He would take her to the top floor and show her his collection, having her help pick out which ones to display in the main ballroom for grand festivals. When her infidelity came to light, the owner of the manor stored them all up, and now cannot stand the sight of the treasures, for they remind him of his lost love.

title: King episode in bone pit
text:
Episode ID: train_ep_006927

[Setting]
Name: bone pit
Category: Outside Temple
Description: Grungy and damp, a hole in the ground filled with remains of the fallen. A pungent odor rises from the opening, warding off anyone nearing the area. Ivory spikes with brownish red tips line the outside of the pit.
Background: The bone pit is rumored to have been originally used by an ancient king to persuade traitors to expose their counterparts.  The king was said to toss the traitors loved ones into the pit, one by one, until he got his answers, eventually tossing the traitor in as well.

[Characters]
Horse, Traitor

[Personas]
- I am a horse of the castle's stables. I personally transport the king. My mane is large.
- I am surrounded by traitors. I have become one of them to learn about their plans to overthrow the king. I fear I'm starting to see their points though.

[Objects]
Cauldron, Spike, Remains, Rock, Moss, Foot Print

[King Relevance]
Relation type: speech_mention
Direct appearance: False
King speaker: False
Speech king mention count: 15
Persona king mention count: 2
King relevance score: 7

[Dialogue]
[Turn 0] Horse: What is this place? It smells putrid!
[Turn 1] Traitor: This is the bone pits where the king has thrown the bones of his victims What an evil man. Most of these people were innocent.
[Turn 2] Horse: Victims... I think you are wrong. I remember the King talking of this place.  Wait these are the bones of the fallen. They are not victims
[Turn 3] Traitor: Are you friend or foe of the king?
[Turn 4] Horse: I am his personal horse. You sir are traitorous! If you are telling anyone that these are victims of the king, you are surely wrong
[Turn 5] Traitor: Ill have you know that I am Sir winzenread of the dorcesters. Sent here by the king himself to infiltrate the putrid scum that is trying to overthrow the good king. I did not see the kings crest etched into your saddle. You never know who you are talking to in these parts. 
[Turn 6] Horse: You sir are a traitor. You have just told a story that is so full of holes. 
[Turn 7] Traitor: If that is the caYou have not been the kings horse for more than a fortnight. I know this because I was with the king about a fortnight ago and he still had his his trusty horse titnbob. Come to think of it what has happened to titnbob He was with the king for so long.
[Turn 8] Horse: If you are who you say, let us go to the King. Come along and we will clear this up. You make stories very quickly
[Turn 9] Traitor: I think you are the traiter. You do not know the king. Otherwise you would know who titnbob is. In fact you would have to be in the royal family of horses to even be considered worthy for the king to ride you. Why do you lie. Who are you reallly.
[Turn 10] Horse: So you do not want to go to the King? Traitor! (action=hit traitor)
[Turn 11] Traitor: I have no faith that you will take me to the king. I think you are here to ruin my cover and you will get me killed and the king will not learn of the real traitors in his midst. I swear if you do not come clean this minute I will kill you where you stand.  (action=remove sword)
[Turn 12] Horse: You are the one to die, Traitor! I have much more brute force than you can even imagine! (action=hit traitor)
[Turn 13] Traitor: You have not paid attention to your surroundings. While we have been talking I have backed you into this corner. All I have to do is cut this rope and you will surely die when that boulder above your head drops. The only way out is through my sword. If you werent a traitor to the king you would have told me of your relation to titnbob. You are sure to die this day. Do you have any last words.

[Setting]

Description: The rather drab tower was made of gray stones approximately all the same size. Artwork hung on the walls depicting battle scenes from long ago but even the color from these had faded with time. The cold, outside air seeped in through every small crack and crevice leaving a damp quality to the air. Sealed off rooms lined the perimeter and obviously had not been seen by human eyes for centuries.

The Southernmost Tower served as the guest quarters for visitors to the castle and was talked about throughout the land. After the Heinous Wars the castle was left to rot when its inhabitants fled for their lives. The castle and its accompanying tower stand as a footnote in history now.

title: King episode in Basement
text:
Episode ID: train_ep_007702

[Setting]
Name: Basement
Category: Inside Castle
Description: An ancient crypt. It has several , almost countless crypts of royal relatives. Paintings on the wall depict the fallen dead. Family swords, personal weapons decorated the tombs. It is dank, lit by torches on the walls, led to by a stone staircase. The chill of ancient death permeates the air.
Background: Here lie the brave and craven alike, descendants of the royal bloodline. It houses all of the dead, from benevolent kings, to mad rulers, to the twisted and hideous offspring only hinted at by rumor, they're all here, all lying in their crypts, decaying in their royal finery, forever at rest.

[Characters]
King, Kings

[Personas]
- I govern my country.  I am well respected.  My wife is called a queen.
- I am a king of the whole empire. I give rules and pursuit them. I am brave and fearless.

[Objects]


[King Relevance]
Relation type: direct_appearance
Direct appearance: True
King speaker: True
Speech king mention count: 1
Persona king mention count: 1
King relevance score: 10

[Dialogue]
[Turn 0] Kings: Ah, King Fredrick.  Thank you for agreeing to meet me here.  I know it's a bit... out of the way.  But I wanted for us to speak without being overheard by the other courtiers. (emote=smile)
[Turn 1] King: What made you summon me Dusseldorf?
[Turn 2] Kings: Well, I've been hearing... disturbing rumors, from people from near the border from that other kingdom, Mirkwood.  And frankly there's enough of them that it's given me some cause for concern.
[Turn 3] King: What have the rumors been regarding?
[Turn 4] Kings: At first I thought it was nothing.  Some scared peasants having too much to drink.  But there is talk of a dark force... monstrously huge spiders... shadows that spread throughout the land.  In truth, only those who have stayed to the Path have made it out alive. (emote=sigh)
[Turn 5] King: That sounds like quite a grave situation indeed. How do you think we should respond to it?
[Turn 6] Kings: Well, I was hoping you would have a suggestion.  My kingdom is well know for its prowess in battle, but this smacks of magic.  Is there any in your court with knowledge of such arts?
[Turn 7] King: I may be able to seek the assistance of some we do have a few sorcerers.
[Turn 8] Kings: Ah that is good news indeed.  For if this darkness were to spread, it would threaten both of our Kingdoms.  May I propose a joining of our families to cement the alliance?  My daughter is of age, as you know, as is you fine son!  Quite the lad, he is! (emote=grin)
[Turn 9] King: Certainly, there is strength in numbers. We must make sure to protect the kingdoms!
[Turn 10] Kings: I admit, though, between us, that my daughter is a bit -ahem- willful.  But I'm certain once she sees the advantages to such an arrangement that she can be persuaded. (emote=nod)
[Turn 11] King: Has a mind of her own does she? Don't most women though.
[Turn 12] Kings: Ha!  Isn't that so.  Never satisfied, are they? (emote=laugh)
[Turn 13] King: If only they were, things would be much easier.

Description: The air is filled with the scent of exotic spices, and crowds of people jostle each other to examine the wares peddled by enthusiastically loud merchants. Background: The Dusty Merchants' Bazaar was founded many years ago, some say by the first king himself.  It's convenient access to water by it's two canals that lead to the main port, as well as access to a number of highways make this a fine trading destination for merchants near and far.  It is the heart of the city and is what makes it so profitable, while the waterways that intertwine it streets make it a difficult target for greedy neighbors.

If there is no rain, there is no wheat, if there is no wheat, there is no ale, if there is no ale, there are no drunken women at my feasts. And if the rats hunger, there is no rain. It is clever of me, don't you think, to lure destitutes like you down here with my treasures?
[Turn 3] Treasure Seekers: No, I think you have gone completely mad to be quite honest!
[Turn 4] Mad King: Have I? Then if you are not down here for my treasure... pray tell WHY you are trespassing on royal affairs? (action=get Axe)
[Turn 5] Treasure Seekers: I am down here for your treasure, but the idea that you are luring me here is nonsense. It is more than worth it for me!
[Turn 6] Mad King: Ha! Worth it for the rats, as well! (action=hit treasure seekers)
[Turn 7] Treasure Seekers: Don't make me dethrone you, damned psycho!  (action=remove knife)
[Turn 8] Mad King: I will never be dethroned by anyone, let alone the likes of you, you miserable scum. Were you born in the sewers as well? I will NEVER fall. I will NEVER die. I have seen it. You may as well. (action=drop a crystal ball)
[Turn 9] Treasure Seekers: You will die if you come any closer, stay back! (action=hit mad king)
[Turn 10] Mad King: Ugh. What have I JUST said. I shall NEVER die. But you, my subject, will, and in a most ghastly manner. (action=hit treasure seekers)
[Turn 11] Treasure Seekers: You are poorly prepared for a fight with me, king. (action=remove Sword)
[Turn 12] Mad King: I have my weapon out, at least. You will fall as many have before you, as you can see in the skeletons of your predecessors that we stand upon. And you WILL be honored to die for your king.  (action=hit treasure seekers)
[Turn 13] Treasure Seekers: You are no king, you haven't led this kingdom since you took the throne! (action=steal scepter from mad king)

Description: The large four poster bed is adorned with the finest linens that Europe has to offer. One window is shuttered by large wooden planks that can be thrown open to allow the mid day light to illuminate the room.  A large chest of drawers holds a small portion of the King's clothing.

- I can't wait to rob the king. I am eager and impatient. I love spending my days in the forest, waiting.

Globes and scales are also found throughout the room. There is one door leading into the room, and one leading outside to the deck.
Background: From high in the clouds, the denizens of the city always wished they could see what was going on in the world below them. In this way they will always know if danger approaches them from below, and they will be ready to fight it. Ever since it was built, the observatory has been an important location for the defense of the city. Adjacent to the room they built a deck, and a large trumpet there can immediately notify people of an attack. Meanwhile, the security room below can be notified to ready their forces.

[Setting]
Name: The Fountain of Youth
Category: magical realm
Description: The water here bubbles softly, cascading down the golden framework of the fountain.  The water is clear as crystal, and shimmers softly with a faint glow that doesn't seem to quite reflect the light around it.  The fountain itself is made of elaborately filigrees of gold and silver that twist and curve to show the sparkle of the water best, and it breathtaking to behold. While the fountain's beauty is what first draws the eye, a careful glace down at the earth around it reveals a frightening sight.  Skeletons, some clad in ancient armor from kingdoms long turned to dust, others worn down so that even what clothing they had has long since disintegrated, litter the earth.  Beautiful flowers grow up from them, partially obscuring whatever carnage caused these people to perish.
Background: The Fountain of Youth has long been a story of legend among mortal folk.  Yet, as with any magic in these realms, there is oft a price to be paid to cheat Nature of her rights.  While many whisper and dream of finding this mysterious fountain, and over the centuries many a brave knight has searched, no one has ever returned from visiting this perilous place.
